summary: pallet-revive's EVM transaction decoder misclassifies unrecognized typed-transaction bytes as legacy transactions instead of rejecting them, deviating from the specification and producing inconsistent transaction validity between pallet-revive and spec-compliant EVM implementations.
details: The specification reserves a distinct byte range for typed-transaction identifiers, separate from the range used to signal legacy transactions. pallet-revive's decoder only recognizes the transaction types it actually implements, and treats any other value, including undefined typed-transaction identifiers, as a legacy transaction rather than rejecting it. As a result, a payload that a spec-compliant EVM implementation would reject as invalid can instead be accepted and decoded by pallet-revive, producing inconsistent transaction validity between chains and complicating tooling such as cross-chain bridges that assume consistent transaction interpretation.

database_specific.title: Pallet-revive misclassifies unrecognized typed transactions as legacy
